name: Chen Baozhen
current_role: Co-founder and major (5%+) shareholder of Wangsu Science & Technology (ChinaNetCenter), Shenzhen-listed 300017; not an executive
profile: Chen Baozhen co-founded the predecessor of Wangsu Science & Technology, a Shanghai CDN/edge-computing and internet infrastructure provider, in 2000 after ~30 years at a Fujian electrical-instrument factory. She sold much of her stake in 2018-2020 and further reductions were announced in 2024; she remains a 5%+ holder.
interesting_fact: She started her career in 1960 at an electrical instrument factory in Fujian and stayed 30 years before co-founding what became one of China's largest CDN / data-center service companies at around age 60.

public_contacts.value: Wangsu investor Q&A via Shenzhen Stock Exchange Hudongyi platform (stock code 300017) / p5w IR platform

notes: Very private; no interviews found. Wangsu (CDN/edge/data centers) is highly relevant to a data-center podcast, but the operational leaders are chairman Li Boyang and board secretary Zhou Liping; route any request via Wangsu's board office. Search usage limits limited depth.

name: Meyer "Micky" Malka
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Ribbit Capital (Palo Alto); director of Robinhood Markets
profile: Venezuelan-born fintech investor who started and sold companies in Venezuela, co-founded Brazil's Banco Lemon (sold to Banco do Brasil) and mobile-payments firm Bling Nation/Lemon (sold to LifeLock, 2013), then founded Ribbit Capital in 2012. Ribbit was an early backer of Robinhood, Coinbase, Credit Karma and Nubank; Malka sits on Robinhood's board and Ribbit is a 10%+ holder of Root Inc.
interesting_fact: Ribbit's name comes from the sound a frog makes, meant to evoke 'leapfrogging' incumbent financial institutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he co-founded Heptagon Group, a brokerage serving Venezuelan and U.S. markets, and co-developed Patagon.com, later acquired by Banco Santander; he also co-founded Banco Bracce, a Brazilian lender to mid-sized companies.
notes: Holds an economics degree from Universidad Catolica Andres Bello (Caracas). Has appeared on the Founders podcast (David Senra) — a good sign he does long-form audio. Ribbit site lists no public email; best route likely via Ribbit or Robinhood corporate communications.

name: Li Denghai
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Shandong Denghai Seeds (SZSE 002041); chairman since 2025 is Tang Shiwei
profile: Li Denghai, a farmer's son from Laizhou, Shandong, is known as the 'father of compact hybrid corn' in China. He founded Houdeng Agricultural Experiment Station in 1985 (China's first private corn-seed enterprise), which became Denghai Seeds, listed in Shenzhen in 2005. In his late 70s he remains active as founder/honorary chairman.
interesting_fact: He set China's summer-corn yield record seven times and the world record twice, including 1,402.86 kg per mu with 'Denghai Chaoshi No.1' in 2005; his compact hybrids once covered ~43% of China's corn acreage. He and Yuan Longping are dubbed 'Southern Yuan, Northern Li'.
deep_cut_fact: After junior high in 1966 he went back to farm in Houdeng Village; at 23 (1972) he became head of the village agricultural-science team, and from 1978 spent winters breeding in Sanya, Hainan to squeeze two generations a year out of his corn lines.
notes: Emails are the company's board-office (dmb) and general mailbox as listed in the 2025 annual report. Attended the Feb 2025 private-enterprise symposium in Beijing. Agriculture rather than energy/data centers; likely Chinese-language interview only.

name: Yuan Jinyu
current_role: Chairman (since Sept 2000), Shenzhen Sunlord Electronics Co. (SZSE 002138)
profile: Yuan Jinyu (b. 1956) has chaired Sunlord Electronics since its founding in 2000; it listed in Shenzhen in 2007 and is a leading Chinese maker of chip inductors, magnetic components, RF/microwave parts and sensors. Sunlord is now pushing into data-center and AI-server power components (vertical-power inductors, tantalum capacitors) and automotive electronics.
interesting_fact: Sunlord's 2025 annual report names data centers/AI servers as a key growth driver: its magnetic components and tantalum capacitors go into GPU boards, ASICs and AI-server power modules, and it also cites fuel-cell/energy-storage applications for data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before electronics he spent a decade (1982-1992) as manager of a supply-and-marketing company under Shenzhen Automobile Industry Corp., then ran Shenzhen Sanjiu (999) Electromechanical Equipment Co. from 1993 to 2004.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center angle (AI-server power magnetics). Low public profile; president Shi Hongyang is the operating face of the company. Email is the board-office/investor mailbox in the annual report.

name: Li Guiping
current_role: Co-actual controller of Changjiu Logistics (SSE 603569) and Changjiu Holdings (HKEX 6959); executive director/chair/GM roles at Changjiu Co. and Guangxi Changjiu Auto Investment
profile: Li Guiping and her husband Bo Shijiu (Changjiu chairman) jointly control the Changjiu group, which grew from Jilin into one of China's largest finished-vehicle logistics providers (Changjiu Logistics, listed in Shanghai) and an auto dealership business, Changjiu Holdings, listed in Hong Kong in January 2024.
interesting_fact: The Changjiu group spans the car value chain: Changjiu Logistics moves finished vehicles for automakers, while Changjiu Holdings (6959.HK, IPO Jan 2024) runs auto dealerships; Li and Bo are co-controllers of both.
notes: Very low public profile; husband Bo Shijiu is the public face (chairman, logistics-association roles). Best route is the company's board office mailbox. Little personal biographical info is published.

name: Wang Chuan
current_role: Xiaomi co-founder; no confirmed current executive role (stepped down from remaining Xiaomi subsidiary posts by July 2025)
profile: Wang Chuan founded KTV song-system maker Leishi (Thunderstone) and e-reader software firm Duokan, which Xiaomi absorbed in 2012, making him one of Xiaomi's eight co-founders. He led Xiaomi TV/smart-home businesses and became Xiaomi China president in late 2018, then gradually stepped back; in 2025 he left his last legal-representative roles at Xiaomi entities.
interesting_fact: Leishi, the KTV song-selection system he founded and controlled, once held about 40% of China's KTV-system market; running it gave him the appliance supply-chain experience he later brought to Xiaomi hardware.
deep_cut_fact: In the Kingsoft years Lei Jun asked him to become Kingsoft CEO; he declined, agreeing instead to be a nominal executive director who came in two days a week (reportedly often four). He is a self-described Apple fan who idolised Steve Jobs' minimalism.
notes: Very low-profile; even Leishi employees reportedly didn't recognise him. No published personal or office contact found; any approach would have to go via Xiaomi corporate communications. Search budget limited this entry.

name: Ivan Xu
profile: Listed by Hurun (2018-2021) for Trendy International Group (Hekki/赫基, owner of Ochirly, Five Plus, Trendiano). Trendy's founder and chairman/CEO is Jacky Xu (徐宇), who founded it in 1999 with Coral Li; a separate 'Ivan Xu' appears in filings as a former Trendy executive director. Could not determine which person the Hurun entry means.
notes: Identity ambiguous: Hurun's 'Ivan Xu' may be a romanisation of founder Jacky Xu (徐宇) or a different executive. Verify before outreach; if it is Jacky Xu, background in CKGSB profile https://english.ckgsb.edu.cn/story/jacky-xu-founder-of-the-fashion-empire-trendy-international-group/ . Apparel, not an energy/data-center fit.

name: C. Alexander Harman
current_role: Managing Partner, J.F. Lehman & Company (JFLCO); Non-Executive Director, DPC Holdings Ltd (Doncasters) since Feb 2026
profile: Alex Harman is managing partner of J.F. Lehman & Co., a New York private-equity and credit firm focused on aerospace, defense, maritime and infrastructure, sitting on its management and investment committees. He joined from J.P. Morgan's Global Energy Group (natural-resources and utility M&A). JFLCO-backed Doncasters (DPC Holdings) IPO'd in 2026; he sits on its board.
interesting_fact: Doncasters makes precision-cast superalloy parts for jet engines and industrial gas turbines; its 2026 prospectus pitches IGTs as a play on surging power demand from data centers and AI — a direct energy/data-center angle.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated cum laude in history from Williams College, and chairs JFLCO portfolio companies CodeMettle, NorthStar Group, TMS Group and Wellman Dynamics while also serving on the board of cargo airline Atlas Air Worldwide.
notes: The ~$766M SEC-insider figure likely reflects JFLCO fund holdings in DPC attributed to him as a director/fund principal, not purely personal wealth. Best route: JFLCO general inquiry mailbox.

name: Yang Yingchun
current_role: Co-actual controller (with son Yang Le) of Anhui Jinhe Industrial (SZSE 002597); chairman of Anhui Jinrui Investment Group
profile: Yang Yingchun (b. 1964) chaired Anhui Jinhe Industrial from 2009 to 2019 and still chairs its parent, Jinrui Investment Group, through which he and Yang Le control ~46% of Jinhe. Based in Lai'an County, Chuzhou, Jinhe is a major global producer of food sweeteners such as sucralose and acesulfame-K, plus basic and fine chemicals.
interesting_fact: Jinhe describes itself as a major global player in sweeteners; it grew out of a Lai'an County fertilizer plant's formaldehyde venture (Wandong Jinrui Chemical, ~2001) into one of the world's big sucralose/acesulfame suppliers.
notes: Holds a master's degree. Operating leadership has passed to Yang Le (chairman). Very low media profile; route via Jinhe board office mailbox. Fertilizer-plant origin: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2011-06-21/b8b1a241-7866-4ef8-8fb5-9363f70ea730.PDF

name: Wan Renchun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen VMAX New Energy (Group) Co. (SSE STAR 688612)
profile: Wan Renchun founded Shenzhen VMAX, which makes power-domain electronics for new-energy vehicles: on-board chargers, DC/DC converters and integrated powertrain-domain units for Chinese and global automakers. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023; he remains chairman and actual controller.
interesting_fact: VMAX's chargers support bidirectional/inverter functions, letting EVs act as mobile distributed energy-storage units — an angle the company highlights as a key industry trend (vehicle-to-load/grid).
notes: Good EV power-electronics/energy fit. Personal background is sparsely published; full CV is in the STAR Market prospectus (2023). Route via VMAX board office.

name: Ke Binghua
current_role: Vice Chairman and Vice President, Keboda Technology Co. (SSE 603786); co-actual controller with chairman Ke Guihua
profile: Ke Binghua (b. 1969, Hong Kong permanent resident) co-controls Shanghai-based Keboda Technology, an automotive-electronics supplier of lighting controllers, motor controllers, energy-management and on-board electrical products for global automakers. The Wenzhou-rooted company listed in Shanghai in 2019; chairman Ke Guihua is the other co-controller.
interesting_fact: Keboda grew from Wenzhou electrical-component roots into a Tier-1 auto-electronics supplier whose lighting and energy-management controllers ship to major German and Chinese carmakers.
notes: Low profile; chairman Ke Guihua is the company's public face. Route via Keboda board office email.

name: Lin Peiqing
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Sirio Pharma Co. (SZSE 300791), Shantou
profile: Lin Peiqing (b. 1965, master's degree) built Shantou-based Sirio Pharma into a leading contract developer/manufacturer of nutrition and dietary-supplement products (soft gels, gummies, tablets) for global brands. Sirio listed in Shenzhen in 2019 and in 2023 bought control of U.S. maker Best Formulations; he remains chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: By 2025 revenue Sirio says it is No. 3 globally and No. 1 in China among nutrition-and-health food solution providers, and the world's second-largest gummy and softgel supplement solutions provider.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sirio he was deputy director of the Shantou Jinshi Pharmaceutical General Factory, a state pharma plant, before becoming chairman and GM of Sirio's predecessor company.
notes: Consumer health, not energy. Company has a U.S./Europe presence so English-language outreach via the corporate site may work. Search budget exhausted; facts from 2025 annual report.

name: Xu Jingen
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Kunshan Kersen Science & Technology (SSE 603626); controlling shareholder
profile: Xu Jingen founded and controls Kunshan Kersen Science & Technology, a precision metal and plastic structural-parts maker (die-casting, CNC, MIM, laser welding) for customers such as Apple, Huawei, Amazon, Google, Meta and Medtronic. Its medical-device unit (Kersen Medical) was sold for RMB 915m in Dec 2025, leaving consumer electronics, auto/EV and energy-storage PACK modules.
interesting_fact: Kersen's parts go inside smartphones, laptops, VR headsets and foldable hinges, and until 2025 also in scalpels, bone screws and pacemaker components; it now also makes energy-storage PACK modules.
notes: Hurun classifies under 'medical equipment' (Kersen Medical), but that unit has been divested. Low public profile; route via board office. Search budget exhausted, limited personal background.

name: Nishita Shah Federbush
current_role: Director and largest individual shareholder, Precious Shipping PCL (SET: PSL); managing director, GP Group (Thailand)
profile: Nishita Shah is a Bangkok-based businesswoman of Gujarati descent who took over GP Group, the family conglomerate spanning shipping, aviation, healthcare, software, hospitality and construction. Its flagship holding is Precious Shipping, one of Thailand's largest dry-bulk shipping lines, founded by her father Kirit Shah in 1989 and listed in 1993.
interesting_fact: Alongside running a shipping-led conglomerate, she owned clothing company Burn Baby and launched her own fashion label, '-Nsha-', sold on three continents.
deep_cut_fact: She is a Boston University graduate and was named in a 2008 Times of India piece on Gujaratis in Forbes' 'GenNext' young billionaires list.
notes: Precious Shipping's site blocks automated access, so no IR email was captured; its IR page and the SET filings list company contacts. Current board status not re-verified after 2022 (search budget exhausted).

name: Michael A. Newhouse
current_role: Co-President, Advance (Advance Publications); independent director, Charter Communications (since 2016)
profile: Michael Newhouse (66) is co-president of Advance, the Newhouse family's private holding company whose portfolio includes Conde Nast, Advance Local, American City Business Journals, The IRONMAN Group, Turnitin and Stage Entertainment. Advance holds ~13% of Charter Communications and is among Reddit's largest shareholders; he represents it on Charter's board, bringing cable programming and infrastructure experience.
interesting_fact: Through Advance, his family business owns The IRONMAN Group, the world's largest operator of mass-participation sports, alongside Conde Nast and a big Reddit stake.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Tufts University graduate and sits on Charter's Nominating & Governance and Finance committees, where his board role centres on cable programming and cable infrastructure expertise.
notes: Newhouse family is famously private; Advance communications is the right channel. Deep-cut fact is thin (from proxy); search budget exhausted before finding interview material.

name: Tang Yongqing
current_role: Former chairman and co-actual controller of Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe (SSE 601028); no current listed-company role found
profile: Tang Yongqing founded Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe in Wuxi in 1999 and chaired it through its Shanghai listing, making welded steel pipe (LSAW, SSAW, ERW) used mainly for oil and gas transmission lines and structural steel. The family later exited; the listed shell became Shandong Yulong Gold and voluntarily delisted in 2025.
interesting_fact: Yulong's line pipe went into oil and natural-gas transmission, and by 2014 it had developed corrosion-resistant pipe for oil/gas gathering lines, coal-chemical plants, power-station heat exchangers and seawater-desalination systems.
deep_cut_fact: He set up the company in December 1999 with RMB 8 million (80% of capital) — RMB 2 million in cash plus RMB 6 million of net assets he took over from the old Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe Group — registered in Wuxi's Huishan district.
notes: Off the rich lists since 2017; listed company changed hands and was delisted in 2025, so old Yulong contacts are stale. No current published contact found. Oil/gas pipe gives a loose energy angle. Search budget exhausted.

name: He Yongyu
current_role: Former director (2010-2013) of Vtron Technologies (SZSE 002308) and of its holding companies Vtron Investment / Vtron Group; no current role found
profile: He Yongyu (Hong Kong resident, b. c.1953) was one of the He family co-controllers of Guangzhou-based Vtron Technologies, a maker of DLP large-screen 'video wall' display systems for control rooms, which listed in Shenzhen in 2009 and was led by chairman He Zhengyu. She left Vtron's board in Dec 2013, matching her 2010-2013 Hurun listings.
interesting_fact: Vtron specialised in ultra-high-resolution tiled display walls (DLP splicing walls) used in command and control centres such as power-grid, traffic and public-security dispatch rooms.
notes: Off rich lists since 2013; very low profile. Vtron was later delisted (2024), so no live corporate channel exists. Not recommended as a priority target.

name: Huang Bingliang
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Zhang Xiaocheng, 50/50 via Qingdao Kangdien Industrial) of Qingdao Vland Biotech (SSE 603739)
profile: Huang Bingliang co-controls Qingdao Vland Biotech, which makes industrial and feed enzymes, probiotics (microecological products) and animal-health products. Vland's management is drawn heavily from Shandong Liuhe Group, the feed giant that merged into New Hope Liuhe in 2011, which likely explains Hurun listing his wealth source as 'New Hope'; that link is inferred, not confirmed.
interesting_fact: Vland's enzymes and probiotics sell into feed, food, textiles and other industries, making it one of China's notable listed industrial-enzyme producers.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: the Hurun entry says 'New Hope'; the only filings match for this name is Vland's co-controller, whose company has deep Liuhe/New Hope Liuhe ties. Verify before outreach. Search budget exhausted.
